prompt:
I need the front end for Lessonbound. Enrollment and billing software for small independent music schools, which staff use to sign students up for a term of lessons, commit tuition and payment plans, and process withdrawals and refunds under the school's policy.

Who's using it: Marisol Grant, office manager at Riverbend Music Studio, a school with 11 teachers and about 230 students. The owner picked this software for the whole staff. Marisol handles enrollment, billing and families' questions at the front office, and she is the person who has to get the money right.

What they're doing right now: It's the last day of early enrollment for the Winter 2027 term. The Pereira family is on the phone signing up three children: piano for Sofia (9), violin for Mateo (12) with Ms. Chen, who has only two Tuesday slots left, and a beginner group guitar class for Lucas (7). Marisol needs to hold the lesson slots, apply the sibling discount and the early-enrollment rate, set up the three-installment plan the parents chose, and charge the first installment to the card on file once they confirm. Ten minutes later the father calls back: Lucas wants to wait until spring. She needs to withdraw him within the 7-day free-cancellation window, release his place in the class, and refund the right part of the installment.

What's in the system at this point: Winter 2027 term: Jan 11 – Mar 20, 10 weeks. Rates: private 30-minute lessons $340 per term, 45-minute lessons $480, group guitar (max 6 students) $210; early-enrollment discount 5% until Nov 16 at 11:59 pm; sibling discount 10% on the second and later children; registration fee $25 per family. Policy: full refund within 7 days of enrollment; after that, prorated by weeks remaining minus a $40 fee. Teacher availability: Ms. Chen (violin) has Tue 4:15 and Tue 5:45 open; Mr. Abara (piano) has 6 open slots; Saturday 10:00 group guitar has 2 of 6 spots left. Pereira family account: parents Ana and Rui Pereira, Visa ending 4471 on file, a $0 balance, 2 past terms enrolled. Payment plan: 3 installments (Nov 16, Dec 15, Jan 15). Earlier today's transactions: 14 enrollments, 2 withdrawals, $6,920 collected.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
